claims.title: Cost-sensitive adaptive Boolean queries obey an exact stop-versus-experiment Bellman recursion
claims.scope: finite Boolean hidden models with rational query costs, deterministic coordinate observations, Bayesian terminal coding loss, and a finite query budget
assumptions: query costs are paid when the query is taken
terminal loss is posterior minority probability
nonclaims: query costs are declared decision costs rather than physical resource costs

claims.title: A query can be dynamically optimal even when querying it and immediately stopping is strictly worse than stopping now
claims.scope: finite-horizon adaptive experiment problems with future query choice contingent on the current observation
assumptions: future experiment scheduling may depend on current query outcomes
nonclaims: negative myopic value does not imply negative dynamic value

claims.title: Uniform three-bit multiplexer has exact equal-cost dynamic query threshold one quarter
claims.scope: uniform three-bit multiplexer, two-query budget, equal rational cost c per coordinate query
assumptions: the selector is queried first in the two-step contingent plan
terminal K3 Bayes gap without information is one half
nonclaims: the threshold is specific to this finite construction

claims.title: Three-bit parity stops immediately under any positive query cost when only two queries remain
claims.scope: uniform three-bit parity with two-query budget and strictly positive coordinate query costs
assumptions: every proper subset leaves parity balanced
nonclaims: full three-query access can still determine parity

claims.title: Bounded exact cost-sensitive adaptive query audit
claims.scope: multiplexer thresholds, negative-myopic-value option value, zero-cost boundary, and parity stopping tests
assumptions: all values use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded tests are not a scalability theorem
CI success is not evidence for simulation
